citation.author: McManus, Denis
citation.title: Affect and Authenticity: Three Heideggerian Models of Owned Emotion
citation.in: Hadjioannou, C. (ed.), Heidegger on Affect, Philosophers in Depth (Palgrave Macmillan)

discipline: philosophy (Heideggerian phenomenology in dialogue with analytic philosophy of action, ethics, and moral psychology)
thesis: Examines what authenticity (Eigentlichkeit/'ownedness') in one's affective life could mean for Heidegger by staging three rival models -- the decisionist model (authenticity as a radical, groundless choice of one's values), the standpoint model (authenticity as the consistent owning of a vocation, project, norm-set, or narrative), and McManus's own preferred All-Things-Considered Judgment Model (ATCJM, authenticity as non-evasive responsiveness to the full plurality of one's concrete normative situation) -- and argues only the third survives the objections the first two face. Chapter authored by Denis McManus; Hadjioannou is the volume editor only. Never mentions boredom (Langeweile) anywhere in its 25 pages; its FCM citations (pp.64, 66, 67-68, 283) are drawn from FCM's general prefatory account of Stimmung/attunement, not from the specific three-form boredom typology.

sections.title: The elusiveness of affective authenticity; the Eigentlichkeit/'authenticity'-vs-'ownedness' translation dispute; the three models previewed

Heidegger on Affect -- I: Befindlichkeit and Stimmung -- Withy's observation that owned emotion is under-discussed; the 1924 BCAP gardener example; the 'Promethean' worry (Cooper) that authenticity's individualizing requires standing apart from Dasein's inescapable Gestimmtsein

The Decisionist Model -- Friedman's reading of authenticity as a groundless, thoroughgoing choice; applied to affect: emotions are 'own' only if freely (groundlessly) chosen; SZ 169-170 on das Man prescribing Befindlichkeit

Heidegger on Affect -- II: Disclosive Submission to a World That Matters -- affect as 'a primordial kind of Being for Dasein' disclosing prior to cognition/volition; Heidegger in Bordo's 'recessive' anti-denigration tradition with Aristotle/Hume/Nietzsche; affect as precondition of intentionality itself

Criticism of the Decisionist Model Reframed -- Murdoch/Tugendhat: a groundless choice is one 'it was not I who chose'; McManus's extension: decisionist 'liberation,' read through Gestimmtsein, is affective stasis/paralysis, not Promethean freedom

The Standpoint Model -- authenticity as owning a vocation/project/norm-set/narrative (Varga, Crowell, Kukla, Haugeland, Guignon); affective correlate via Varga's righteous-indignation example and Rudd's 'serious ethical agent'; McManus's student-essay-mark counterexample

Normative and Emotional Pluralism -- real lives subject to many competing norms/roles at once; the standpoint model's 'subtler Prometheanism'; Varga's 'openness to change' clause does not resolve the pluralist intuition

The All-Things-Considered Judgment Model -- authenticity as responsiveness to all aspects of one's situation at once (ATCJ); the Moore's-paradox-style argument; grounding in Heidegger's readings of Aristotelian phronesis and of 'guilt' (Schuld)

Owning Emotions and All Things Considered -- answers Blattner's over-intellectualization objection; ATCJ requires emotional openness; inauthenticity as 'evasive turning-away' (SZ 136); rugby-practice/friend's-worries example; rejects Frankfurt's decision-based ownership account; aligns with Withy's (2015) 'owned affectivity'
Endnotes 1-43, including the flagged anxiety lacuna (n.35), the Frankfurt critique (n.39), and the Withy alignment (n.42)

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: analogical only (P/anticipatory-application) -- boredom is never mentioned; the decisionist model's critique (a will stripped of all mattering 'shuts down' into stasis) structurally parallels the significance-draining that defines monotony/meaninglessness, but McManus draws no such connection himself

constructs.label: Eigentlichkeit / authenticity as ownedness
constructs.treatment: the chapter's central topic; translation dispute between 'authenticity' and 'ownedness' set up at the outset

constructs.label: Befindlichkeit / Stimmung / Gestimmtsein (attunement)
constructs.treatment: the affective-disclosive architecture that all three models of authenticity must accommodate; 'the fundamental way in which Dasein is as Dasein' (FCM 67)

constructs.label: Decisionist, Standpoint, and All-Things-Considered Judgment models of authenticity
constructs.treatment: the chapter's own tripartite construct; ATCJM is defended as the model that survives objections the other two face

constructs.label: normative and emotional pluralism
constructs.treatment: McManus's own diagnostic construct deployed against the standpoint model: real lives are subject to multiple, competing norms/roles simultaneously

constructs.label: guilt (Schuld) / evasion (Ausweichen)
constructs.treatment: grounds the ATCJM's textual case (via Heideggerian 'guilt' and phronesis) and its account of inauthentic affect as an 'evasive turning-away' (SZ 136)

readings.text: Owned emotion is comparatively neglected in the Heidegger-authenticity literature, which follows Heidegger's own emphasis on owned understanding, despite emotion being central to Befindlichkeit and Stimmung. The gardener example (BCAP 131-133) illustrates affective 'tuning'; emotion is a 'being-taken of Dasein... from without,' properly understood as constitutive of being-in-the-world, not passive victimhood.

Inescapable Gestimmtsein generates a standing interpretive problem: what could authenticity's radical individualizing of Dasein be, other than a 'Promethean' standing-apart-from-or-above conditions (absorption-in-the-world, dispersal in das Man) Heidegger elsewhere treats as essential structural features of Dasein (Cooper 1997, 110, 112)?

Decisionist model (Friedman 2000): authenticity is recognizing one's practical context as 'simply one possibility among others,' subject to a 'thoroughgoing' choice resting on 'no taken for granted background framework at all.' Applied to affect: since das Man prescribes one's Befindlichkeit (SZ 169-170), emotions become 'our own' only via free choice of the values/concerns determining how we are moved.

Against the tradition that denigrates affect as a mere 'third class' phenomenon obfuscating thought, Heidegger (in Bordo's 'recessive' counter-tradition with Aristotle/Hume/Nietzsche) argues affect discloses 'a primordial kind of Being for Dasein,' prior to cognition/volition, through which Dasein has 'already submitted itself to having entities... matter to it' (SZ 136-137, 341).

Heidegger allows Dasein can 'become master of its moods' but only 'by way of a counter-mood' -- 'we are never free of moods' (SZ 136). More radically, affect is a precondition of intentionality as such, 'the medium within which' thinking/doing/acting happen (FCM 64, 67-68); 'even the purest theoria has not left all moods behind it' (SZ 138).

Murdoch and Tugendhat: a choice not made in the light of reasons leaves how one chooses 'to accident,' so 'it was not I who chose.' McManus's extension: since being free to choose how to feel requires being stripped of all mattering, decisionist 'liberation' -- read through Gestimmtsein -- is not Promethean freedom but affective stasis: 'when Dasein becomes free in this sense... it shuts down.' No 'subject which merely beholds' can exist apart from all mattering, so the decisionist's presupposed pure chooser is impossible in principle.

Standpoint model (Varga, Crowell, Kukla, Haugeland, Guignon): authenticity is the consistent owning of a vocation/commitment/narrative across contexts. Applied to affect: the authentic person is moved consistently, tracking her owned commitments (Varga's righteous-indignation example; Rudd's 'serious ethical agent' who cannot 'turn off' generosity/compassion between contexts).

McManus's counterexample: a student upset about a low essay mark; acting from consistent generosity/compassion (awarding extra marks) 'doesn't seem right' -- McManus 'ought to be moved by... professionalism and a sense of fairness' instead. The standpoint model lacks the first model's Promethean flaw but harbors a 'subtler form of Prometheanism.'

Real lives are normatively multi-dimensional (son, father, husband, colleague, teammate, etc.) -- no single wholehearted commitment captures this without fancifully renouncing the rest. The standpoint model's subtler Prometheanism is a standing-apart from this essential plurality in favor of one or two commitments. Varga's 'openness to change' clause only licenses replacing one wholehearted project with another (reemplotment), not holding multiple competing commitments open at once, so it does not resolve the pluralist worry.

McManus's own All-Things-Considered Judgment Model (ATCJM): authenticity is responsiveness to all relevant aspects of one's situation at once, not the partial view of a single office/goal/norm -- an 'all-things-considered judgment' (ATCJ). Moore's-paradox argument: '(1) from the POV of goal w, what ought to be done is y' invites 'but what do you think ought to be done?'; '(2) all things considered, what ought to be done is y' does not -- asserting (2) while adding 'though I think z' is self-undermining.

Textual grounding for ATCJM: Heidegger's reading of Aristotelian phronesis (the person who 'bears witness' must 'say what is best,' not merely recommend what is profitable for a goal/role, BCAP 112) and Heidegger's account of 'guilt' (Schuld) -- the finite Dasein 'constantly is not' and has 'waived' other possibilities; 'every action is... marked by guilt' because 'the possibilities of action are limited in comparison with the demands of conscience' (SZ 285; WDR 169).

Objection (Blattner 2013): doesn't ATCJM make authenticity 'too deliberative, too intellectualized,' given deliberation is 'a decidedly secondary phenomenon' for Heidegger? McManus agrees with the premise but argues ATCJ is compatible with it: what is basic is not explicit propositional deliberation but 'the breadth of one's horizon,' one's affective 'range of disclosure.'

Central move: ATCJ requires emotional openness -- acknowledging 'the full range of emotions that my situation elicits,' corresponding to the many ways it matters. Inauthenticity is illustrated by the rugby-practice/friend's-worries example: invoking 'I've got to take care of my family' to evade a friend's worries disguises, rather than resolves, competing normative demands -- an evasion of the needed ATCJ, not a performance of it.

Conclusion: authenticity requires resisting das Man's prescription of 'the possibilities of attunement' and remaining open to the full range of ways one's situation 'summons' one; inauthenticity is 'precisely an evasive turning-away' (SZ 136) from the fullness of one's affective life and the guilt-laden normative pluralism it alone discloses.

Against Frankfurt's view that we 'own' only the emotion corresponding to the demand we decide to act on, dissociating from the rest as 'external to the will,' McManus calls this 'an odd, forced conclusion': un-acted-upon emotions remain 'very much one's own'; what one dissociates from through evasion is making an ATCJ at all. McManus aligns his account instead with Withy's (2015) independent characterization of 'owning affectivity' as resisting 'averageness' and 'holding oneself open' to being moved.

concepts.gloss: standard translation 'authenticity' captures ordinary-German 'real/genuine'; literal 'own-ness' captures eigen ('own,' vs. fremd, 'alien'); McManus uses the standard translation while asking the reader to hear both resonances
disposedness/findingness; the existential structure through which Dasein always already finds itself exposed to a mattering world, not an inner psychological state
mood/attunement/'tuning'; 'the fundamental way in which Dasein is as Dasein' (FCM 67); inescapable ('we are never free of moods,' SZ 136)

Friedman's reading: authenticity as a radical, groundless choice remaking one's normative framework from no background at all; applied to affect, owning emotion requires freely choosing the values that determine how one is moved
authenticity as the consistent owning of a vocation, project, norm-set, or life-narrative across contexts; affective correlate = consistency of emotional response tracking one's owned commitments

McManus's preferred model: authenticity as non-evasive responsiveness to the full plurality of demands one's concrete situation makes, requiring an all-things-considered judgment (ATCJ) rather than a judgment relativized to one role/goal/norm
the fact that real human lives are subject to many competing norms/roles simultaneously (son, father, colleague, teammate, etc.), which no single wholehearted commitment or narrative can capture
the finite creature's inescapable foreclosure, in every action, of other possibilities the 'demands of conscience' would also require; 'every action is... marked by guilt' (WDR 169)
Dasein's everyday non-openness to the full range of its affective disclosedness; the ATCJM's own definition of inauthenticity, via SZ 136

interlocutors.name: Martin Heidegger
interlocutors.role: primary text under analysis, chiefly SZ, FCM, BCAP, HCT, CT, and the Aristotle/phronesis lectures (PS, PICA)

interlocutors.name: Michael Friedman
interlocutors.role: canonical statement of the decisionist reading of Heideggerian authenticity (2000, 51-52), which the chapter constructs and then rejects

interlocutors.name: Iris Murdoch
interlocutors.role: The Sovereignty of Good (1970): objects that a groundless, 'wild leaping' choice is not really a choice at all; radically free will is 'empty,' 'substanceless,' devoid of normative characteristics

interlocutors.name: Ernst Tugendhat
interlocutors.role: Self-Consciousness and Self-Determination (1986): a choice not made in the light of reasons leaves how one chooses 'to accident'; 'it was not I who chose'

interlocutors.name: David Cooper
interlocutors.role: names the 'Promethean' worry -- that authenticity's individualizing seems to require standing apart from or above Dasein's essential structural features

interlocutors.name: Susan Bordo
interlocutors.role: The Flight to Objectivity (1987): locates Heidegger, with Aristotle/Hume/Nietzsche, in the 'recessive' tradition resisting philosophy's denigration of emotion

interlocutors.name: Somogy Varga
interlocutors.role: standpoint-model source: authenticity as 'integrating one's life by wholeheartedly endorsed projects'; righteous-indignation example; 'openness to change' clause examined and found insufficient

interlocutors.name: Anthony Rudd
interlocutors.role: narrativist standpoint-model source: the 'serious ethical agent' who cannot 'turn off' generosity/compassion between contexts; also concedes the pluralist intuition McManus builds the third model from

interlocutors.name: Charles Guignon
interlocutors.role: narrative-identity version of the standpoint model: authentic 'life-course' as 'continuity and constancy,' a 'coherent, cumulative narrative'

interlocutors.name: Christine Korsgaard
interlocutors.role: Self-Constitution (2009): consistency of choice/action as constitutive of having 'your conception of what is worth doing,' cited as an outside-Heidegger instance of the standpoint intuition

interlocutors.name: R. M. Hare
interlocutors.role: The Language of Morals (1952): moral principles are best identified by what one does when faced with genuine choices -- another outside-Heidegger instance of the standpoint intuition

interlocutors.name: Steven Galt Crowell
interlocutors.role: 'owning of norms' as an important theme in his work, cited as another version of the standpoint model

interlocutors.name: Rebecca Kukla
interlocutors.role: alternative standpoint-model account: we own norms 'in virtue of our recognition of their force,' their legitimacy

interlocutors.name: John Haugeland
interlocutors.role: Dasein Disclosed: authentic standpoint as 'critically realized' by finding and rooting out inconsistencies in one's self-understanding; also source of 'no one who simply did not give a damn... could be a proper scientist'

interlocutors.name: David Velleman
interlocutors.role: Kantian unified-point-of-view account cited as an analogue of the standpoint model's constancy requirement

interlocutors.name: Bill Blattner
interlocutors.role: 'Authenticity and Resoluteness' (2013): objects that deliberation is 'a decidedly secondary phenomenon' for Heidegger, pressed against ATCJM's apparent intellectualism

interlocutors.name: Harry Frankfurt
interlocutors.role: rival, decision-based account of owned affect (we 'own' only the emotion corresponding to the demand acted upon, 'dissociating' from the rest as 'external to the will'); explicitly rejected by McManus as 'odd, forced'

interlocutors.name: Katherine Withy
interlocutors.role: 'Owned Emotions: Affective Excellence in Heidegger on Aristotle' (2015): opening observation that most authenticity scholarship focuses on owned understanding, not owned emotion; independent account of 'owning affectivity' as resisting averageness and holding oneself open, which McManus's third model aligns with

interlocutors.name: Alison Jaggar
interlocutors.role: 'outlaw emotions' (1989): emotions that precede conscious recognition that something is wrong with accepted understandings; McManus notes his view differs from but is compatible with Jaggar's stress on caution here

interlocutors.name: Mikko Salmela
interlocutors.role: 'What Is Emotional Authenticity?' (2005): 'integrity view' of emotional authenticity requiring coherent but revisable patterns of emotion, cited alongside the standpoint model's constancy requirement

interlocutors.name: Jean-Paul Sartre
interlocutors.role: named as the likely source of the decisionist reading's popularity, via the 'original choice which originally creates all values and all motives' (1969, 465)

tensions.label: Decisionist vs. disclosive-submission accounts of affect
tensions.poles: authenticity as a groundless choice of the values determining how one is moved (Friedman) vs. Heidegger's own insistence that affect is a primordial disclosure prior to all cognition and volition, to which Dasein has always already 'submitted' (SZ 136-137)

tensions.label: Standpoint-model constancy vs. normative/emotional pluralism
tensions.poles: authenticity as the consistent owning of one or two wholehearted projects/norms/narratives (Varga, Rudd, Guignon) vs. McManus's argument that real lives are subject to many simultaneously competing norms/roles that no single standpoint can capture without a 'subtler Prometheanism'

tensions.label: ATCJM as over-intellectualized vs. as basically affective
tensions.poles: Blattner's objection that talk of 'judgment' and 'consideration' makes authenticity too deliberative for a philosopher who treats deliberation as secondary vs. McManus's reply that ATCJ's basic form is a non-propositional 'breadth of horizon'/emotional openness, not explicit reasoning

tensions.label: Frankfurt's decision-based ownership vs. McManus's evasion-based account of owned affect
tensions.poles: Frankfurt: we own only the emotion corresponding to the demand we decide to act on, dissociating from the rest as 'external to the will' vs. McManus: unacted-upon emotions remain fully one's own; what one dissociates from through evasion is the ATCJ itself, not particular emotions

tensions.label: Anxiety-privileging vs. boredom as an (unexamined) alternative candidate Grundstimmung -- our own observation, not McManus's
tensions.poles: McManus explicitly flags anxiety as the Grundstimmung his three models still owe a full account of (n.35), without raising boredom as a candidate at all, even though this same volume's ch.8 (bor-sec-04) argues profound boredom merits comparable authenticity-disclosing status to anxiety
tensions.locus: p.148 n.35 (P/anticipatory-application -- our own observation, not the chapter's claim)

extraction.note: chapter 6 of 12, extracted from Hadjioannou (ed.) Heidegger on Affect (2019); no boredom content and no FCM-boredom-specific engagement found -- see Reading of FCM section of the .md for the honest negative finding and its significance
